Need 0.0750 mol CuSO4. If using anhydrous CuSO4, mass is about 12.0 g. A strong procedure includes weighing, dissolving in a beaker, quantitative transfer to a 500.0 mL volumetric flask, rinsing the beaker and funnel, filling to the mark, and inverting to mix. Reducing concentration error can include careful meniscus reading at eye level.

Damp filter paper makes the measured product mass too high, so percent yield appears too high. Leaving precipitate in the beaker lowers the collected mass, so percent yield appears too low. Water is suitable because it dissolves the ionic reactants so the ions can mix and form the insoluble precipitate.
